content:
iPhone Bumper cases have been popular with users since the iPhone 4 era, but in recent years there are fewer and fewer options on the market. For users who want a minimalist protective case, Rhinoshield offers a good option.

Apple finally re-entered the bumper case market last year with the iPhone Air. I had originally expected Apple to extend its bumper case to the iPhone 18 Pro (just as they previously expanded the clear case to the iPhone 11), but unfortunately they did not do so. While looking for other options, I came across Rhinoshield's Minimalist Impact Bumper case.

Key Details

The Impact Bumper case has a fit similar to most other bumper cases, with a fairly slight raise at the screen edge and a slightly more pronounced edge at the back. The case has a unique design that I really appreciate, with special support points that keep the camera plateau and lenses from making direct contact with whatever surface the phone is placed on; given that both the 17 Pro and 18 Pro have aluminium bodies, I particularly appreciate this. This makes it significantly more protective than a typical bumper case, while also eliminating that annoying wobble when laying the phone flat on a table.

However, the fit of the case is not entirely to my expectations. It is a bit loose, with edges that can be easily pried outward, and I am concerned that prolonged use may stretch it out. That said, I don't think the phone is likely to fly out of the case if dropped (and I have inadvertently tested this). That said, the entire case is made of hard plastic rather than rubber, so hopefully there will be no issues over the long term. Rhinoshield states that the entire case uses a single material and is therefore 100% recyclable.

The case comes in three colours, all designed to match the iPhone 18 Pro body colours: white, blue, and black (sorry, burgundy fans). The blue I have is close to but not exactly the same as the Glacier colour.

Shortcomings

However, the case does have some drawbacks. My biggest complaint is that the buttons are very difficult to press. For some reason they went with a design that sits almost flush with the body, and the way the buttons are designed makes the pressing feel mushy.

The overall material choice could also be considered a drawback. In my opinion, it feels cheaper than Apple's iPhone Air bumper case, though some people might actually prefer this material. Compared to typical TPU/rubber clear case materials, I definitely prefer this feel. However, this material combined with the looser design seems especially prone to attracting lint from pockets.

If you use Apple's Wrist Strap or Crossbody Strap, please note that this case does not have the required attachment points for a lanyard.

Conclusion

Rhinoshield's bumper case is far from perfect, and I still hope Apple will extend its bumper case to other iPhone models. Ultimately, however, I decided to keep the case, for one main reason: it allows me to enjoy a near-bare experience without worrying about damage or dents to the fragile aluminium body. As far as I know, this bumper case is usually only sold on their own website, priced at around USD 30, which works out to be similar to Apple's pricing (USD 39) once shipping is factored in. You can buy the Rhinoshield Minimalist Impact Bumper case here. (It occasionally appears on Amazon, which is also worth a try.)
